name: KatalIArc domain metamodel
purpose: Describe the domain concepts and relationships used to elicit, reason about, evaluate, review, and record software architecture decisions.
modeling_guidance: Treat this file as the domain vocabulary, not as proof that every concept must have a separate JSON artifact.
A relationship's cardinality is stated only when known; do not infer one from an ambiguous drawing or absent data.
Keep traceability between business goals, requirements, the architectural problem, quality scenarios, alternatives, assessments, and decisions.
Record provenance and distinguish documented evidence, inference or hypothesis, and unknown information.
Distinguish qualitative criterion judgments from verified compliance with a scenario response measure.
Do not infer client priorities. A stakeholder representative must confirm priority values.

Stakeholder.description: A person or group that provides context, has concerns, or confirms priorities or decisions.

BusinessProblem.description: The business or user problem that motivates the architecture work.

BusinessGoal.description: An intended business outcome and, when available, its measure of success.

BusinessRequirement.description: A business-level need or obligation that informs the architectural problem.

ArchitecturalProblem.description: The architecture problem to solve, derived from business context and drivers.

ArchitecturalContext.description: System boundary, team capabilities, technology environment, and other context relevant to reasoning.

ArchitecturalConstraint.description: A restriction that limits acceptable architectural choices.

QualityAttribute.description: A quality concern such as performance, availability, modifiability, or security.

QualityScenario.description: A measurable scenario that makes a quality concern actionable.

ArchitecturalDriver.description: A requirement, quality scenario, or constraint with material influence on architecture decisions.

ArchitecturalKnowledge.description: Knowledge that may inform architectural reasoning; applicability must be assessed for the current project.

ExplicitArchitecturalKnowledge.description: Recorded knowledge such as styles, tactics, patterns, or documented project experience.

TacitArchitecturalKnowledge.description: Experience-based knowledge such as expert heuristics or practitioner judgment; treat as a hypothesis until supported.

ArchitecturalStyle.description: A broad organization of system elements and relationships.

ReferenceArchitecture.description: A reusable reference structure for a domain or class of systems.

ArchitecturalTactic.description: A design decision that influences a quality attribute through a stated mechanism.

ArchitecturalPattern.description: A reusable high-level structure with components and connectors.

ExpertHeuristic.description: An experience-based conditional recommendation, not established evidence by itself.

ProjectExperience.description: A recorded experience from a prior project and its observed outcome.

PatternTacticInteraction.description: How a tactic fits, changes, or is constrained by a pattern.

TacticInteraction.description: A positive, negative, or conditional interaction among tactics and affected scenarios.

ArchitecturalAlternative.description: A coherent candidate architecture assembled from patterns and tactics.

ArchitecturalRisk.description: An uncertain condition that could negatively affect an alternative or decision.

TradeOff.description: A consequence where improving one concern may worsen another.

ScenarioAssessment.description: Six traceable Walton judgments for one complete alternative and one quality scenario.

attributes.criteria: object keyed by C1 through C6 with criterion value, justification, evidence, and assumptions

DecisionRationale.description: The reasons, uncertainties, and evidence supporting a decision outcome.

ArchitecturalDecision.description: A recorded selection or disposition of an architectural alternative.

ArchitectureDecisionRecord.description: A versioned, persistent decision proposal and its approval and retrieval-indexing history. The local JSON and Markdown are authoritative; a vector-store copy is only a retrieval projection.

ADRVersion.description: An immutable version of an ADR proposal with traceable source artifacts.

ADRContent.description: Structured decision content that preserves the evidence chain from business context through assessment and review.

ArchitecturalArgument.description: A traceable argument for an architectural claim using grounds, warrant, backing, qualifier, and rebuttal.

UtilityTreeBranch.description: An index grouping scenario IDs by quality attribute; it does not duplicate scenario details or priorities.

SensitivityPoint.description: An architectural property whose variation may materially affect a quality-scenario response; candidates are explicitly labeled.

CriticalQuestionAssessment.description: A recorded Walton critical question applied to a specific claim, with response and evidence.

EvaluationIteration.description: A bounded Toulmin refinement and Walton reevaluation event; stores artifact-level observations, not private model reasoning.

AlternativeEvaluationResult.description: Deterministic consolidation of all scenario judgments for one alternative and its tactics.

attributes.criteria: object keyed by C1 through C6

ArchitecturalNonRisk.description: A justified absence of a risk under the stated conditions and evidence.

relationships.name: provides_or_is_affected_by
relationships.meaning: Stakeholders provide context about or are affected by business problems.

relationships.name: motivates
relationships.meaning: A business problem motivates one or more business goals.

relationships.name: informs
relationships.meaning: Goals inform business requirements.

relationships.name: contributes_to
relationships.meaning: Requirements contribute to framing the architectural problem.

relationships.name: is_understood_in
relationships.meaning: The problem is considered in its system and team context.

relationships.name: is_limited_by
relationships.meaning: Constraints restrict acceptable solutions.

relationships.name: is_influenced_by
relationships.meaning: Drivers shape the architectural response.

relationships.name: includes
relationships.meaning: Quality scenarios can be architectural drivers.

relationships.name: characterizes
relationships.meaning: Each quality scenario concerns a quality attribute.

relationships.name: indexes_by_id
relationships.meaning: The utility tree groups scenario IDs under quality attributes without copying scenario content.

relationships.name: may_inform
relationships.meaning: Knowledge may inform reasoning; current applicability must be argued, not assumed.

relationships.name: is_a
relationships.meaning: Explicit architectural knowledge is a kind of architectural knowledge.

relationships.name: is_a
relationships.meaning: Tacit architectural knowledge is a kind of architectural knowledge.

relationships.name: includes
relationships.meaning: Explicit knowledge may include architectural styles.

relationships.name: includes
relationships.meaning: Explicit knowledge may include reference architectures.

relationships.name: includes
relationships.meaning: Explicit knowledge may include architectural tactics.

relationships.name: includes
relationships.meaning: Explicit knowledge may include architectural patterns.

relationships.name: may_be_realized_by
relationships.meaning: A style may be represented or combined through patterns.

relationships.name: may_contain_or_inspire
relationships.meaning: A reference architecture may contain or inspire patterns.

relationships.name: participates_in
relationships.meaning: Pattern and tactic fit or change is recorded by PatternTacticInteraction.

relationships.name: participates_in
relationships.meaning: Pattern and tactic fit or change is recorded by PatternTacticInteraction.

relationships.name: contributes_to
relationships.meaning: Pattern/tactic implications can inform the overall interaction analysis.

relationships.name: targets_or_affects
relationships.meaning: Tactics target quality attributes and may affect scenarios positively or negatively.

relationships.name: interacts_with
relationships.meaning: Tactics may interact; effects are recorded in TacticInteraction.

relationships.name: affects
relationships.meaning: Interactions record affected scenarios and consequences.

relationships.name: assembles
relationships.meaning: An alternative assembles zero or more patterns.

relationships.name: uses
relationships.meaning: An alternative uses one or more tactics.

relationships.name: is_assessed_by
relationships.meaning: Alternatives are assessed against quality scenarios.

relationships.name: assesses_against
relationships.meaning: An assessment references the scenario it evaluates.

relationships.name: may_have
relationships.meaning: Alternatives may have risks and trade-offs.

relationships.name: has_tradeoff
relationships.meaning: Alternatives may involve trade-offs.

relationships.name: selects_or_defers
relationships.meaning: A decision selects an alternative or records that selection is provisional or undetermined.

relationships.name: is_justified_by
relationships.meaning: The rationale records justification, uncertainty, and supporting references.

relationships.name: records
relationships.meaning: A decision records the trade-offs it accepts.

relationships.name: records
relationships.meaning: The ADR persists a proposed or accepted architectural decision and its traceable rationale.

relationships.name: has_versions
relationships.meaning: Every revision is preserved as an immutable ADR version.

relationships.name: contains
relationships.meaning: A version contains a structured decision proposal.

relationships.name: traces
relationships.meaning: ADR content references the quality scenarios considered.

relationships.name: records_selected_tactics
relationships.meaning: ADR content records the selected tactics and their sources.

relationships.name: preserves_arguments
relationships.meaning: ADR content preserves the Toulmin arguments.

relationships.name: preserves_assessments
relationships.meaning: ADR content preserves qualitative scenario assessments.

relationships.name: records_risks
relationships.meaning: ADR content records risks and sensitivity points.

relationships.name: records_tradeoffs
relationships.meaning: ADR content records accepted trade-offs.

relationships.name: supports_or_qualifies
relationships.meaning: Arguments support or qualify alternatives and their design claims.

relationships.name: is_a
relationships.meaning: An expert heuristic is a form of tacit architectural knowledge.

relationships.name: is_a
relationships.meaning: Project experience is a form of tacit architectural knowledge.

relationships.name: assesses_alternative
relationships.meaning: Each assessment refers to exactly one alternative and one scenario.

relationships.name: has_candidate_or_supported_sensitivity
relationships.meaning: An alternative may expose properties whose variation affects scenario responses.

relationships.name: is_critically_reviewed_by
relationships.meaning: Critical questions challenge the assessment and its causal justification.

relationships.name: may_be_revised_in
relationships.meaning: Assessment revisions retain traceable iteration history.

relationships.name: consolidates
relationships.meaning: Each alternative result consolidates its scenario judgments by rule priority.

relationships.name: preserves_outcomes
relationships.meaning: A proposed ADR records the calculated action and applied rule for each alternative.
